newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Oct 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Oct 10.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

According to the Industrial Relations Department's second annual report on enterprise bargaining released yesterday, 38 per cent of managers do not believe the process is delivering significant productivity improvements at their workplaces and the rate of productivity improvement is slowing down. Page 1.

The annual report by the Insurance and Superannuation Commission, tabled in Parliament yesterday, revealed there was a rise of almost 450 per cent in the number of enforcement actions taken against superannuation funds in 1995-96 and about A$17 million ha been defrauded or misappropriated from super funds in the past eight years. Page 2.

The Australian Securities Commission will be back in the Federal Court today to try to convince the court to extend a freeze on almost A$10 million in profits from the abnormal trading in TNT securities in the lead-up to the friendly takeover by Dutch grop Royal PTT. The ASC has not found any leads to Mark Booth, one of the investors who traded options over the phone and paid with untraceable cheques. Page 21.

Coles Myer will apply to the Federal Court today to return confidential transcripts of evidence given on oath during the Australian Securities Commission's Yannon inquiry by Coles major shareholder Solomon Lew. Lew and two of his colleagues sued the ASC ast month for releasing the material to Coles, but they are expected to agree to the retailer's move to return the documents. Page 21.

The International Iron and Steel Institute has forecast a five per cent rise in steel consumption in 1997 for Australia, compared with a 3.4 per cent growth rate for the world industry. However, BHP said last night that any rise in domestic consumption nxt year would be more in the nature of a recovery of lost volumes. Page 22.

Waraluck Ltd, Smorgon Steel and Italian engineering and technology group Engitec Impianti Spa have joined in a venture to recover 100,000 tonnes of zinc metal from flume dust which is normally dumped by Smorgon. Engitec will build a turnkey plant on a sie next to Smorgon's Laverton, Melbourne, electric arc furnace steel plant. Page 22.
THE AUSTRALIAN

In an effort to convince the key Indian diamond market that Argyle Diamond Mines intends to remain as an independent force in diamond marketing, ADM managing director Gordon Gilchrist said in Mumbai yesterday there was a natural partnership between Argyle and the Indian cutting and polishing and jewellery manufacturing companies and after three months of successful independent diamond marketing, Argyle saw it as the way of the future. Page 27.

Ansett Australia Holdings' Traveland Pty Ltd now has an estimated 20 per cent of the A$5 billion a year Australian air travel market after buying the retail operations of mid-range operator Travelstrength yesterday. Traveland general manager Graham Perrysaid the purchase would add profits and sales to Traveland while maximising the increase in sales of Ansett tickets. Page 27.

After winning a $10 million contract to build a grain terminal at Fangcheng in the Guangxi autonomous region in south-western China, Australia Wheat Board chairman Trevor Flugge believes the Board is now in a position to win the next contract in the progrm - a A$253 million project at Dalian, also in China's south-west. Page 27.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Bankers Trust Australia's head of Australian equities, Rohan Hadley, yesterday refused to confirm whether Bankers Trust would accept Dutch group KPN's A$2 billion offer for transport giant TNT after BT lifted its stake in the target to almost 20 per cent and said KPN's bid was "at the lower end" of the range of valuations. Page 23.

Although Commonwealth Bank executives assured shareholders at Tuesday's annual meeting that profits would be maintained in 1997, banking analysts are predicting the bank will suffer a fall in earnings, along with the other major banks. CBA shares fell sharply yesterday, finishing at A$11.70, while National Australia Bank, ANZ and Westpac also experienced significant drops in share prices. Page 23. -

-- News Corporation's Foxtel will have a free hand when it comes to negotiating the free-to-air rights to televise Super League games, following confirmation from the Australian Broadcasting Authority yesterday that the games are not covered under the Governent's anti-siphoning laws, which would normally require Foxtel to arrange free broadcasting of one or more live games each week. Page 23.

With four takeover attempts being foiled by rivals in the past 16 months, St George Bank is exploring the possibility of forming an alliance with a foreign institution and is also likely to unveil a A$200 million share buyback and a bonus dividend with its annual result in November. Page 23.

Addressing Opposition concerns that Budget cutbacks to industry assistance would cost jobs, particularly in emerging industries such as computers, Prime Minister John Howard conceded yesterday that Australia needed a stronger rate of economic growth to reduce unemployment. Page 25.

Investor Washington H Soul Pattinson has posted a 28.4 per cent rise in net profit to A$48.3 million for the year to July 31 thanks to a buoyant return from its coalmining operations in Australia and Indonesia. Soul Pattinson was instructed by the Austraian Securities Commission to include profits from its 49.8 per cent-owned Brickworks subsidiary in one set of accounts. Page 25.
THE AGE

Bankers Trust Australia is yet to decide whether it will accept KPN's offer for transport giant TNT, saying that the A$2 billion bid was "at the lower end of our range of valuations". BT has increased its holding in TNT by three per cent to 19.99 per cen since the A$2.45-a-share offer was announced last week. Page B1.

In a bid to end the legal battle with its largest shareholder, director Solomon Lew, Coles Myer is expected today to seek Federal Court approval to hand back transcripts of evidence given by Lew and two of his associates unread. The

In a bid to end the legal battle with its largest shareholder, director Solomon Lew, Coles Myer is expected today to seek Federal Court approval to hand back transcripts of evidence given by Lew nad two of his associates unread. The transcripts contain evidence given to the Australian Securities Commission during the inquiry into the Yannon transaction. Page B1.

After predicting two years ago that Australia would be on the brink of financial collapse by 1997 with an insoluble level of debt, interest rates rising and the currency in decline, IBIS Business Information head Phil Ruthven now says that Australia is faing a gradual decline into a genteel poverty for the rest of the decade. Page B1.

Plans by Australia's largest advertising agencies, George Patterson Bates, Saatchi & Saatchi and The Campaign Palace, to combine their buying power under the umbrella of Zenith Media Australia will give the new group billings totalling A$1 billion. Page B.

Australian Wheat Board chairman Trevor Flugge said yesterday that the Board's success in gaining a A$10 million contract with the Chinese Government showed that relations with China are very good. The Wheat Board will build a grain storage depot in Fang heng City in a consortium with construction company Transfield. Page B3.

The Australian Securities Commission has granted Southcorp Wines relief under the Corporations Law to allow it to wrap up its A$12 million takeover bid for Coldstream Australasia. The ASC's national takeovers coordinator, Nigel Morris, said that without he modification Southcorp would not have been able to move to full control of Coldstream within the existing time frame of its offer. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
